title: phase-shift-throughput-sweep-lab-notes-juno
content:
Goal:
Small personal lab to understand how alternating request-phase offsets between two synthetic tenants affects effective throughput and tail latency under the continuous-batching runtime. Wild hypothesis: certain phase offsets create pathological batching collisions that reduce effective batch utilization and amplify p99 by orders of magnitude.

Setup summary:
- Model: trimmed-7b (local dev compile, int8-ish profile enabled)
- Hardware: 1x A100S (40GB) dev node, CUDA 11.8, runtime branch: phase-batcher-experiment (local changes)
- Load generator: custom Go harness + wrk-style driver that can control phase offset deterministically
- Workload: two tenants (A and B) each sending 75 RPS; request size ~32 tokens prompt + 64 max gen; seq len ~96 avg
- Runtime config: dynamic batching on, max_batch=16, batch_window_ms=6, kvcache enabled, per-tenant rate limiting disabled for the test
- Run length: 10 minutes per phase offset, 2 warm-up minutes (not included in stats)

Commands (approx):
- go run ./bench -model trimmed-7b -rpsA 75 -rpsB 75 -phase-offset 0.0 -dur 10m -out run-0.csv
- iterate phase-offset from 0.0 to 0.95 by 0.05

What I measured (primary metrics):
- overall throughput observed (tokens/s and requests/s)
- batch utilization (avg batch size seen by runtime)
- p50, p90, p95, p99 for request latency (end-to-end from send to final token)
- GPU utilization and SM% sampled at 1s cadence

Key raw numbers (representative window, trimmed medians across minute 3-9):
- phase=0.00: req/s total=150, tokens/s=~18k, avg batch size=11.6, p50=47ms, p90=122ms, p95=210ms, p99=390ms
- phase=0.25: req/s total=150, tokens/s=~17.2k, avg batch size=9.1, p50=62ms, p90=180ms, p95=370ms, p99=950ms
- phase=0.48: req/s total=127 (dropped effective throughput), tokens/s=~14.3k, avg batch size=6.3, p50=92ms, p90=420ms, p95=820ms, p99=2.1s
- phase=0.50: req/s total=151, tokens/s=~17.8k, avg batch size=10.2, p50=49ms, p90=130ms, p95=240ms, p99=460ms
- phase=0.75: similar to 0.25 but slightly worse p99 (~1.1s)

Observations / interpretation:
- There is a non-monotonic relationship between phase offset and tail latency. Offsets around ~0.48 caused the worst-case behavior in these runs.
- Hypothesis: when the relative offset aligns so that arrivals from tenant B consistently fall just shy of batch_window boundary opened by tenant A, we end up with many underfilled micro-batches that still trigger kernel startup/launch overheads, killing amortization.
- Avg batch size correlates strongly with p99; when avg batch size < ~7 the p99 explodes (2s+ observed).
- phase=0.5 is surprisingly benign (it interleaves nicely, forming fuller batches). The pathological point is slightly off the perfect interleaving point (likely because of small jitter + deterministic scheduling).
- GPU SM% drops in pathological windows, indicating the device is underutilized due to batching inefficiency (not compute-limited).

Quick reproducibility notes:
- Re-running with jitter injected at client (~±2ms) smooths the extreme peaks: p99 reduced by ~60% at the pathological offset but average throughput slightly lower. This suggests a practical mitigation (client-side micro-jitter).
- Increasing batch_window_ms from 6 -> 12 eliminated the worst p99 but increased median by ~25ms (tradeoff: latency vs tail).
- Enabling aggressive prefix caching (for repeated prefixes) did not materially change the phase effect for these synthetic prompts.

Follow-ups and TODOs:
- [ ] Re-run the sweep with 3 tenants (A, B, C) to see higher-order phase interactions (esp. 3-way offsets).
- [ ] Profile runtime at pathological offset with nvprof/ Nsight to capture kernel launch gaps and CPU wait times.
- [ ] Add a run where requests have variable lengths (5%-95% quantile spread) to simulate real traffic and check sensitivity.
- [ ] Push a small runtime patch that randomizes per-request batch deadline by ±1ms and benchmark again (low cost mitigation).
- [ ] Write a short internal note for runtime-team with suggested mitigations (client jitter, adjustable batch window heuristics, deadline randomization).

Open questions / discussion prompts:
- If we implement jitter at bridge/load-balancer level, what's the effect on cost (slightly more latency; fewer p99 spikes)? Worth for enterprise customers with strict p99 SLAs?
- Can the batcher be made aware of tenant-level phasing and actively schedule to avoid pathological alignments? Cost to complexity?

Attached artifacts in drive/grafana:
- grafana panel: phase-shift-throughput (linked above) contains the sweep charts and per-tenant batch-size heatmap
- raw CSVs: run-phase-*.csv (stored in /tmp on the dev node for now)

Notes to self (less formal):
- this is fun — nice to finally see a clear geometric effect from micro-scheduling.
- document a short reproducible script and drop into the runtime bench repo so others can iterate without sshing into my node.
- pick a couple of customer traces to replay (if allowed) to see whether real traffic ever hits these corners.

End of notes.

-- Juno
